source_text:
Μὴ οὖν ἀναισθητῶμεν τῆς χρηστότητος αὐτοῦ. ἐὰν γὰρ ἡμᾶς μιμήσηται καθὰ πράσσομεν, οὐκέτι ἐσμέν. διὰ τοῦτο, μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ γενόμενοι, μάθωμεν κατὰ Χριστιανισμὸν ζῆν. ὃς γὰρ ἄλλῳ ὀνόματι καλεῖται πλέον τούτου, οὐκ ἔστιν τοῦ θεοῦ.
ὑπέρθεσθε οὖν τὴν κακὴν ζύμην, τὴν παλαιωθεῖσαν καὶ ἐνοξίσασαν, καὶ μεταβάλεσθε εἰς νέαν ζύμην, ὅ ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός. ἁλίσθητε ἐν αὐτῷ, ἵνα μὴ διαφθαρῇ τις ἐν ὑμῖν, ἐπεὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ὀσμῆς ἐλεγχθήσεσθε.
ἄτοπόν ἐστιν, Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν λαλεῖν καὶ ἰουδαΐζειν. ὁ γὰρ Χριστιανισμὸς οὐκ εἰς Ἰουδαῖσμὸν ἐπίστευσεν, ἀλλ’ Ἰουδαϊσμὸς εἰς Χριστιανισμόν, ᾧ πᾶσα γλῶσσα πιστεύσασα εἰς θεὸν συνήχθη.
thought_title: Live as Christians, not as Jews
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Magnesians, urging them to abandon old ways and live fully as Christians in Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Not therefore let us be without feeling of the kindness of him. For if he should imitate us according to what we do, no longer are we. Through this, disciples of him having become, let us learn according to Christianity to live. For he who by another name is called more than this, is not of God. Put away therefore the evil leaven, the one having grown old and having turned sour, and change into new leaven, which is Jesus Christ. Be salted in him, so that not may be corrupted anyone among you, since from the smell you will be convicted. Absurd it is, Jesus Christ to speak and to Judaize. For the Christianity not into Judaism believed, but Judaism into Christianity, into which every tongue having believed into God was gathered together.

choices.english: let us not be without feeling
choices.why: The verb means to lack perception or feeling; rendering it as 'be without feeling' preserves the literal sense of insensibility toward God's kindness.
The verb means to set aside or remove; 'put away' captures the command to discard the old leaven.
The verb is rare and refers to leaven becoming sour or acidic; 'turned sour' conveys the spoiled state of the old leaven.
The passive imperative of ἁλίζω means to be seasoned with salt; 'be salted' keeps the literal image of preservation in Christ.
The adjective means out of place or absurd; 'absurd' conveys the logical contradiction Ignatius sees in speaking of Christ while Judaizing.
The verb means to live according to Jewish customs; 'to Judaize' is the standard English term and matches the glossary's 'Judaism'.

bible_refs.note: ὑπέρθεσθε οὖν τὴν κακὴν ζύμην, τὴν παλαιωθεῖσαν

pass_b_english: So let us not be numb to His kindness. For if He should deal with us according to what we do, we no longer exist. Therefore, since we have become His disciples, let us learn to live according to Christianity. For whoever is called by any other name than this is not of God.

Put away, then, the evil leaven, which has grown old and turned sour, and change into new leaven, which is Jesus Christ. Be preserved in Him, so that no one among you may be corrupted, since by your fragrance you will be recognized.

It is absurd to speak of Jesus Christ and to Judaize. For Christianity did not come to faith through Judaism, but Judaism through Christianity, in which every tongue that has believed in God has been gathered together.

last_rejected.why: ἐσμέν = 'we are,' not 'we exist.' Context: if God imitates our evil, we cease to be His people/Christians.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐσμέν means 'we are'; 'we no longer exist' is a valid rendering of ceasing to be, within normal range.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'Ἰουδαϊσμός' as 'Judaism' but this is the verb form; 'Judaize' is standard English for ἰουδαΐζειν and not banned.
last_rejected.ruling: ἰουδαΐζειν is the verb form; 'Judaize' is standard and not the glossary entry Ἰουδαϊσμός.

problems.quote: since by the smell you will be convicted
problems.why: 'Smell' as metaphor for moral detectability is odd; likely from 'be recognized by your scent/character'.
problems.fix: Consider 'by your odor' with note, or 'by your character'.

edits.old: since by the smell you will be convicted
edits.new: since by your odor you will be convicted

problems.quote: For Christianity did not believe in Judaism, but Judaism believed in Christianity, in which every tongue that has believed in God has been gathered together.
problems.why: Grammatically odd: 'Christianity' and 'Judaism' as agents of belief? Personified abstractions confuse the theological claim.
problems.fix: Add note: compressed argument that Jewish prophets/predecessors pointed forward to Christ, not vice versa.

problems.quote: For if He should imitate us according to what we do, we no longer exist
problems.why: Logic is unclear: why would God imitating us cause nonexistence?
problems.fix: Likely means 'if God treated us as our deeds deserve'; retranslate accordingly.

edits.old: For if He should imitate us according to what we do, we no longer exist.
edits.new: For if He should treat us according to what we do, we no longer exist.

edits.old: For Christianity did not believe in Judaism, but Judaism believed in Christianity, in which every tongue that has believed in God has been gathered together.
edits.new: For Christianity did not come to faith through Judaism, but Judaism through Christianity, in which every tongue that has believed in God has been gathered together.

problems.quote: For whoever is called by any other name beyond this is not of God
problems.why: 'beyond this' is unclear; likely 'besides this' or 'other than this'.

problems.quote: your odor you will be convicted
problems.why: 'Odor' for Greek 'osme' likely means 'reputation' or 'fragrance'; 'convicted' is harsh.
problems.fix: 'by your fragrance you will be recognized'.

edits.old: by any other name beyond this
edits.new: by any other name than this

edits.old: since by your odor you will be convicted
edits.new: since by your fragrance you will be recognized

fixed: Changed 'beyond this' to 'than this' for clarity, matching the comparative sense of πλέον τούτου.
Changed 'odor' to 'fragrance' and 'convicted' to 'recognized' to better convey ὀσμῆς and ἐλεγχθήσεσθε in context.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening phrase as 'numb to His kindness' for natural modern English, kept 'Christianity' as the work brief requires, and retained 'Be salted in Him' as a biblical image while ensuring the surrounding sentence reads smoothly.

notes.why: Abstract noun 'Christianity' appears twice; reader may not grasp this is rare early usage.
notes.fix: Note that 'Christianity' as abstract noun is unusual and significant.

notes.why: 'Salted' is biblical (Mark 9:49) but rare; means 'preserved' or 'seasoned.'
notes.fix: Note biblical allusion; or 'be seasoned with salt in him.'

polish.changed: Clarified 'Be salted in Him' as 'Be preserved in Him' to convey the intended sense of preservation from corruption, while keeping all claims and references intact.

notes.why: Archaic or obscure; 'salted' means 'preserved' or 'seasoned', but modern reader may not understand.
notes.fix: Add note: allusion to Mark 9:49/Col 4:6, meaning 'be preserved/purified'.
